 Shri Kaushal Sisodiya, Advocate for the appellant.

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri H. S. Rathore, Government Advocate for the respond
Shri Rajkumar Donawat, Advocate for the respondent No.2/Objector.

Heard on I.A No.10617/2025, which is second application under Section 430 of Bnss for grant of
suspension of sentence filed on behalf of appellant -
Deepak.

2. The appellant has been convicted u/S 376(3) and 376(2)(n) of Ipc and sentenced to undergo Ri
for 20 years with fine of Rs.1,500/- and Ri for 20 years with fine of Rs.1,500/- respectively with
usual default stipulations, vide judgement of conviction and order of sentence dated 20.07.2024
passed by the Special Judge, Pocso Act, Jawad, District Neemuch in Sc No.03/2019.
3.  As per prosecution case, the appellant had abducted the minor girl and also committed rape upon her.
It is clear that prosecutrix herself had gone alongwith the appellant and traveled with him to different places and stayed together for about 10 days and she was also a consenting party.
It is further argued that the prosecution has also failed to prove the source of recording the age of the prosecutrix in the scholar register.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as counsel for the objector have opposed the prayer and submit that age of the prosecutrix has been found to be between 15 to 16 years.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the statement of prosecutrix and also the fact that as per prosecution witness, the 2 CRA-9167-2024 source of recording the age of prosecutrix in the scholar register was school transfer certificate but it has not been proved that on what basis, date of birth of prosecutrix was recorded in school transfer certificate.

In the case of Tijubai @ Omvati Bai and Others Vs. State of M.P. reported in 2025(1)
MPLJ (Cri.)75, it has been held that if the prosecution does not prove the source of date of birth Deepak vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27229302/
1 recorded in scholar register and the same is recorded on the guess, the same cannot be the basis for conviction.

sentences.text: 6. Considering the same, the present application is allowed.

The jail sentence of appellant Deepak is suspended upon his depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 11.11.2025 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Registry.
7. With the aforesaid, I.A No.10617/2025 is allowed and stands disposed of.
8. In view of aforesaid, IA No.10618/2025, which is an application for urgent hearing stands disposed of.
